Mtatsminda Park and Funicular

A hilltop amusement park above the city, reached by a 1905 funicular, with the widest panorama of Tbilisi.

Time needed
3 h
From Tbilisi
6 km · 0:20
Road
Paved
Car needed
Economy class
Season
All year
Entry
ფუნიკულიორი ~6 ₾

Mtatsminda is the roof of Tbilisi. From the ridge at 727 metres the whole city unfolds: the line of the Mtkvari, Narikala, the Sameba cathedral and the Trialeti mountains on the far horizon. It is the one place where the actual scale of Tbilisi becomes obvious.

The funicular opened in 1905 to a Belgian design and still runs on its original alignment. There are three stations: the lower one on Chonkadze Street, an intermediate stop at the Mtatsminda Pantheon, where Ilia Chavchavadze, Akaki Tsereteli, Niko Pirosmani and the Russian writer Griboyedov are buried, and the upper station inside the park.

The park itself is several things at once:

  • A Ferris wheel built right on the edge of the ridge, which puts the view underneath you
  • Rides and carousels for children, plus small themed zones
  • Restaurant terraces that are the best sunset seats in the city
  • Woodland paths for anyone who wants to escape the noise of the fairground
  • The television tower, floodlit at night and used by locals as a navigation point

In winter part of the park keeps working, though some rides close. The view, on the other hand, is far sharper in cold air than in the summer haze.

Practical advice

Arrive about two hours before sunset and you get the daytime city, the golden hour and the night city in a single visit. Rides are paid with a rechargeable card bought at the entrance, so load enough if you are with children. The ridge is windy and four to six degrees cooler than the centre — bring a jacket even in summer. Queues for the funicular are long on weekend evenings, so driving up can actually be faster. Toilets and cafés are inside the park.

How to get there from Tbilisi

There are two ways up. The first is the funicular from Chonkadze Street, leaving your car in the surrounding streets. The second is to drive the Mtatsminda switchbacks from the Vake or Turtle Lake side: narrow but fully asphalted, about twenty minutes from the centre, with a large free car park at the top. In winter the climb can be awkward when the surface ices over, so after snowfall the funicular is the reliable option. In normal conditions an economy car handles the road without any trouble.
